transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-20
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Ariel Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), June Park (Redwood CSM), Dr Leila Hassan (Sienna Bio Head of ML), Tommy Park (Platform Eng), Rhea Singh (Procurement)
Links shared: committed-capacity-deck (https://redwood.com/decks/committed-capacity), SOC2 artifacts link (redacted), EU-region-POC-template (internal link)

Auto summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Sienna Bio is evaluating a 12-month contract extension with committed GPU capacity and EU region onboarding. Key concerns: latency targets for inference pipelines, data residency for patient-adjacent datasets, KMS/HSM integration, and price per token under committed capacity. Redwood AE/SE to provide SKUs, run EU POC with latency/throughput bench, and share security artifacts. Procurement needs contract template and vendor onboarding steps.

Transcript:
[00:00:02] Ariel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we know it's late over there Leila, appreciate you making time. I'm Ariel from Redwood, I'll run through the agenda, Marco will cover the POC and perf questions, and June can talk ops and the SOC2 and onboarding.
[00:00:18] Dr Leila: Thanks Ariel, yeah it's fine. We wanted this call to line up procurement and engineering to see if we can lock an extension and expand into EU for compliance reasons.
[00:00:30] Tommy: Quick note — our downstream pipelines need 95th percentile latency under 120ms for short text inference, otherwise we cascade timeouts.
[00:00:37] Marco: Got it, Tommy. That's helpful. We'll highlight the dedicated capacity profiles that meet that SLA. Quick question, is the workload mostly short sequence (<128 tokens) or are there longer runs?
[00:00:48] Dr Leila: Mostly short but with occasional longer summarizations up to 512 tokens — about 10% of requests.
[00:00:56] Ariel: Cool. For committed capacity we have two SKUs that customers usually pick — one optimized for low latency, one for balanced throughput/cost. We'll send the exact numbers.
[00:01:05] Rhea: From procurement side I just want to flag that Sienna needs a 12-month minimum with termination notice windows and renewal pricing lanes. Also we need to ensure data residency language for the EU region.
[00:01:17] June: We can include residency clauses and region-specific data handling; our private deployments support VPC and on-prem for strictly regulated datasets. I'll share the checklist.
[00:01:28] [00:02:00] Speaker 6: um (inaudible)
[00:02:06] Marco: Alright, on the technical side — for EU onboarding we recommend a shortbench POC. We'll provision a dedicated pool in eu-west and run your typical traffic shape for 48 hours so we can show 95/99 p99 latencies and token cost under committed config.
[00:02:20] Dr Leila: Perfect. Do you have any differences in kernel selection / quantization for EU vs US infra? We care about model parity.
[00:02:31] Marco: No, same runtime and model variants. The only delta is underlying hardware mix in region, but we'll pin to the same model family and quantization profile used in prod. There might be slight perf variance due to perf distro on the host, but we'll show the numbers.
[00:02:45] Tommy: When you say pin, does that mean we can guarantee same weights and exact model sha? We need reproducibility for our audits.
[00:02:53] Marco: Yes you can pin model version. There's a model catalog id and we support deterministic rollouts. The transcript here — sorry — as someone said earlier, sometimes the auto transcript shows KV cash instead of KV cache, so ignore typos.
[00:03:06] Ariel: On pricing, two levers: committed capacity (reserved GPUs) which lowers token cost, and routing policy that can fall back to cheaper region variants when latency budget allows. For Sienna's low-latency pipeline we'll probably recommend a reserved low-latency SKU.
[00:03:20] Rhea: We need committed rates documented in a format our finance team can attach to a PO.
[00:03:25] Ariel: We'll send a pricing sheet with SKU lines, monthly and annual invoicing options and an example PO template.
[00:03:32] [00:04:10] Dr Leila: Side question — can Redwood integrate with our KMS? We use HashiCorp Vault and we need HSM-backed key usage for production keys.
[00:04:20] June: We support KMS integrations and can do HSM-backed customers keys for Private. For Hosted and Dedicated we also offer customer-managed keys integration — there's an additional compliance review for HSM. We'll provide the onboarding runbook.
[00:04:34] Tommy: What's the expected lead time to bring up a dedicated pool in eu-west? If we sign by end of month we want to be live in 3 weeks for the POC.
[00:04:44] Marco: Typical lead time is 2-4 weeks depending on capacity allocations. If you commit to a reserved pool we can prioritize, so 2-3 weeks is possible.
[00:04:52] Rhea: That timing is tight but doable. We'll need a signed order by 03/26 to make the March POC.
[00:04:58] Ariel: Noted. We'll aim for sending the contract draft by 03/24 so you have time for legal review.
[00:05:05] [00:06:00] Speaker 2: uh okay
[00:06:12] Dr Leila: Another point — latency vs cost tradeoff — can we do hybrid: keep low-latency dedicated for critical pipelines and route bulk async traffic to a cost-optimized pool?
[00:06:23] Marco: Absolutely. We support per-route routing policies and can attach route-level SLOs. So critical endpoints get dedicated low-latency; batch jobs hit cheaper quantized variants. We can demo this during the POC.
[00:06:36] Tommy: How about model quantization? For our biomedical models we saw small quality regressions with aggressive 4-bit quantization. Is Redwood able to recommend quant profiles per workload?
[00:06:47] June: Yes our Optimize team provides quant recommendation by workload and we run quality regression tests against your eval set. That's part of the onboarding offering.
[00:06:57] Rhea: Legal will want fallback language in the SLAs — like when Redwood can't meet latency due to region-level capacity issues what's the default fallback?
[00:07:07] Ariel: We have automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants or cross-region fallback. For mission-critical flows you can enable multi-region replication and active-passive routing; we'll document the expected RTO/RPO.
[00:07:18] Dr Leila: OK, for audit we also need detailed request logging and immutable audit trails. Is that available for Dedicated?
[00:07:26] June: Yes, Dedicated and Private include detailed audit logs and longer retention as an add-on. We'll share our logging retention and sample log schema.
[00:07:34] [00:08:00] Marco: Quick technical nit — when you run the POC please share your client-side connection profile, egress patterns, and token utilization distribution. That helps us set batching and KV cache heuristics.
[00:08:10] Tommy: We'll pull that together. There's a small chance we can't share raw patient PII datasets out of region — some of the data needs to stay in EU. We'll mark those requests for EU-only routing.
[00:08:21] Ariel: We can set per-route residency and ensure those tokens never leave eu-west.
[00:08:25] Rhea: Procurement question — do you support quarterly invoicing or only monthly/annual for committed?
[00:08:31] Ariel: We support monthly and annual. Quarterly isn't common for committed capacity but we can discuss a tailored plan for enterprise customers.
[00:08:39] [00:09:10] Dr Leila: How do you measure cost per inference? Will you give us token-level breakdown for the POC?
[00:09:16] Marco: Yes the console gives token and latency breakdown per request/route. For the POC we'll export a spreadsheet with aggregated 95/99 pcts and cost per 1k tokens.
[00:09:25] Tommy: Also confirm whether the EU pool uses the same pricing units or if there's a regional surcharge.
[00:09:31] Ariel: There can be slight regional adjustments for cloud infra costs; we'll show both US and EU pricing lanes in the SKU sheet.
[00:09:38] Rhea: We'll need a clause for energy/price fluctuation? Our procurement team sometimes asks for a cap.
[00:09:43] Ariel: We can add a capped uplift clause for infra taxes — we'll put a typical formula in the draft.
[00:09:49] [00:10:40] Speaker 1: (crosstalk)
[00:11:05] Dr Leila: On the technical side, what about model version rollbacks? We can't afford a bad rollout to affect production.
[00:11:12] Marco: We support canary rollouts and instant rollbacks. There's a model pin and rollout policy you can control via the API/console; plus automatic regression alerts tied to your eval set.
[00:11:21] Tommy: Good. For the POC, can we test failover by simulating node outages?
[00:11:26] Marco: Yes we'll run a resilience test during the POC and measure failover times.
[00:11:31] [00:12:00] June: I'll attach the SOC2 artifact link — note the certificate and last audit report — and also the on-prem deployment checklist for your infra team.
[00:12:09] Rhea: Please mark any items that require Sienna legal signoff.
[00:12:14] June: Will do.
[00:12:20] Ariel: Alright let me recap the commitments — we'll send SKUs + contract draft by 03/24; Marco will provision EU POC and run perf tests and share a spreadsheet by 03/30; June will send SOC2 artifacts and the on-prem checklist by 03/22. Customer to confirm datasets that must remain in EU by 03/26 and procurement to provide PO template by 03/25.
[00:12:40] Rhea: That timeline works for us.
[00:12:45] Dr Leila: One more ask — can you include an appendix in the contract that lists the exact hardware and expected p95/p99 under the committed SKU? We need to attach that to our internal risk assessment.
[00:12:57] Ariel: Yes we'll include an appendix with expected throughput/latency by model and sequence length.
[00:13:04] Tommy: If things go well we'd like to explore APAC provisioning later this year. Can we lock a capacity uplift option in the contract?
[00:13:12] Ariel: We can add an option for an uplift at pre-agreed pricing tiers. We'll include that as a contract line item.
[00:13:19] [00:13:50] Dr Leila: Great. Any risks we should call out now?
[00:13:55] Marco: Primary risk is regional capacity constraints during peak or pre-commit windows; second is rare regressions from quantization on biomedical models. We'll mitigate with dedicated pools and conservative quant profiles.
[00:14:06] Rhea: For legal, the second risk is vendor substitution. We'll want a clause about not changing core runtime or provide notice for breaking changes.
[00:14:15] Ariel: We'll add a notice and change management clause.
[00:14:21] [00:15:00] Speaker 3: (typing)
[00:15:10] Dr Leila: Ok I'm comfortable proceeding with the POC. Let's pencil in the 03/30 benchmark.
[00:15:17] Marco: I'll send a calendar invite for the POC kickoff and include the perf template.
[00:15:22] Ariel: And I'll share the draft contract and pricing after this call.
[00:15:28] Rhea: We'll circulate our procurement template and legal contact.
[00:15:33] June: I'll share the security artifacts now.
[00:15:40] Ariel: Any final questions?
[00:15:45] Tommy: Just one small thing — can we get a sample audit log entry format? We need to map it to our SIEM.
[00:15:52] June: Yes will include sample log schema in the artifacts.
[00:15:57] Dr Leila: Thank you all. Looking forward.
[00:16:00] Ariel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the notes and next steps.

Call end: 16:16 UTC (approx)
